questions.stem: A FortiGate neighbor stays Active and debug reports 107. Which protocol exchange has not completed?

choices.text: The TCP three-way handshake to peer port 179
choices.feedback: Correct: Active plus error 107 marks an incomplete TCP handshake before BGP OPEN can begin.

choices.text: The BGP OPEN capability negotiation between peers
choices.feedback: OPEN follows TCP establishment; an OPEN failure occurs after the transport socket exists.

choices.text: The first UPDATE carrying accepted prefixes for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: UPDATE exchange is later; prefixes cannot be exchanged before the session is Established.

choices.text: The route-map evaluation for received networks for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Route maps govern route policy after BGP messages arrive; they do not complete TCP transport.

questions.stem: The route to a BGP peer exists, but capture shows repeated SYN packets without SYN-ACK. What should be checked next?

choices.text: The inbound prefix-list permit sequence for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: A prefix list is evaluated for route updates, not for the missing TCP response.

choices.text: The return route and any filter for TCP/179
choices.feedback: Correct: the missing SYN-ACK points to the remote return path, an ACL, or a listener/filter problem.

choices.text: The maximum-prefix threshold on received routes for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Maximum-prefix is enforced after routes are exchanged and cannot explain an incomplete handshake.

choices.text: The route-map set-local-preference action for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Local preference is assigned to received routes after BGP reaches the update stage.

questions.stem: A multihop eBGP peer is reachable through a routed core. Which neighbor settings address the local source and hop behavior?

choices.text: Set passive and change the router ID for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Passive changes who initiates a session; it does not select the intended local source or permit multihop.

choices.text: Set route-map-in and soft-reconfiguration for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Route-map and soft-reconfiguration affect route processing, not TCP source identity or TTL.

choices.text: Set update-source and enable multihop with a suitable TTL
choices.feedback: Correct: update-source selects the local source; multihop and TTL allow the routed peer distance.

choices.text: Set next-hop-self and remove the remote AS for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Next-hop-self changes advertised next-hop attributes; the remote AS is required for eBGP identity.

questions.stem: The debug shows 104, Connection reset by peer, rather than 107. What does that change in the diagnosis?

choices.text: It proves the local route table is empty
choices.feedback: A reset does not establish that the local route table is empty; inspect the packet path.

choices.text: It proves a route-map rejected every prefix for this BGP peer
choices.feedback: Route-map rejection cannot be inferred from a transport reset before route exchange.

choices.text: It proves BGP reached Established and lost keepalives
choices.feedback: Established-state keepalive loss is a later failure and would show a different state history.

choices.text: It indicates the remote side reset the TCP attempt
choices.feedback: Correct: 104 indicates the peer or an intermediary reset the connection during the attempt.

questions.stem: FortiManager installs a profile to a 2 GB FortiGate and the preview includes udp-not-quic. What is the most useful first comparison?

choices.text: Compare generated CLI with that model's FortiOS parser support
choices.feedback: Correct: the defect is a manager-generated attribute unsupported by the target model/build.

choices.text: Compare the destination address object with the firewall policy
choices.feedback: Address matching is unrelated to whether the target recognizes a CLI node in an SSL profile.

choices.text: Compare the device HA priority with the ADOM revision
choices.feedback: HA priority and ADOM revision do not determine parser capability for this command.

choices.text: Compare the administrator GUI theme with the install owner
choices.feedback: GUI appearance and task ownership have no bearing on target-side command support.

questions.stem: Why can an SSL/SSH profile save successfully in FortiManager but fail on one FortiGate during install?

choices.text: The manager skipped the device route lookup on this target model
choices.feedback: Route lookup is not the relevant validation boundary for a syntax rejection.

choices.text: The target parser lacks this option on that build
choices.feedback: Correct: manager-side schema validity does not guarantee target model/build support for every CLI option.

choices.text: The firewall policy has no matching destination service
choices.feedback: Policy service matching does not explain a parser rejection in the SSL/SSH profile subtree.

choices.text: The device DNS cache has not refreshed QUIC records
choices.feedback: DNS cache state does not affect whether the FortiGate accepts a configuration command.

questions.stem: Which distinction matters when reviewing the FortiOS SSL/SSH profile fields?

choices.text: quic and udp-not-quic are interchangeable block controls on this target model
choices.feedback: The fields have different protocol meanings; treating them as aliases can change inspection behavior.

choices.text: https and dot share one global action with no separate context
choices.feedback: FortiOS exposes separate https and dot subtrees, so the actions are not one global value.

choices.text: quic handles QUIC; udp-not-quic handles matched UDP that is not QUIC
choices.feedback: Correct: udp-not-quic is the action for matched UDP traffic that is not QUIC.

choices.text: udp-not-quic controls TCP fallback after a QUIC handshake on this target model
choices.feedback: TCP fallback behavior is not what the udp-not-quic field defines.

questions.stem: A workaround works on one target but makes capable models lose intended inspection behavior. What does this suggest?

choices.text: The entire ADOM must be downgraded immediately on this target model
choices.feedback: Downgrading the ADOM may create wider compatibility issues and is not the first response.

choices.text: The manager should stop validating every install on this target model
choices.feedback: Validation is needed to expose target differences; disabling it hides evidence.

choices.text: The FortiGate routing process is rewriting the profile
choices.feedback: Routing does not rewrite SSL/SSH profile attributes during installation.

choices.text: The workaround is too broad; scope it by model
choices.feedback: Correct: use a device/model-scoped override and verify affected and unaffected targets.

questions.stem: FortiAnalyzer's Azure output profile validates, but no rows appear in Log Analytics. Which object is still required to activate forwarding?

choices.text: Attach a Remote Server to the saved output profile
choices.feedback: Correct: the profile must be selected by a Remote Server forwarding setting using the output plugin.

choices.text: A second FortiAnalyzer ADOM revision for the custom table
choices.feedback: An ADOM revision does not activate log forwarding or reference the output profile.

choices.text: A FortiGate central SNAT map for the DCE address
choices.feedback: SNAT may be part of network reachability, but it does not attach the forwarding profile.

choices.text: A FortiSwitch VLAN mapping for the Azure workspace
choices.feedback: Switch VLAN mapping has no role in the FortiAnalyzer-to-Azure plugin configuration.

questions.stem: Why does the Azure custom-table transform create TimeGenerated from logtime?

choices.text: Azure requires the source field to be named logtime
choices.feedback: logtime is only the sample source field; the destination requirement is a separate column.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer only sends timestamps in local time in this ingestion path
choices.feedback: Time conversion is performed by the DCR transform; the requirement is not simply local time.

choices.text: The DCR must create TimeGenerated from logtime
choices.feedback: Correct: the DCR transform creates the mandatory TimeGenerated field from the source timestamp.

choices.text: The DCE uses TimeGenerated as its client secret
choices.feedback: The DCE URL and application secret are separate settings; TimeGenerated is a schema field.

questions.stem: Which six values does the FortiAnalyzer Fluentd Azure profile require?

choices.text: Workspace name, firewall serial, ADOM name, source port, log type, and username
choices.feedback: These are not the documented Azure Logs Ingestion parameters for the Fluentd profile.

choices.text: Tenant ID, client ID, client secret, DCE URL, DCR ID, and table name
choices.feedback: Correct: those are the six required parameters listed in FortiAnalyzer's example.

choices.text: DCR name, device ID, interface name, time zone, proxy port, and token cache
choices.feedback: Device and interface inventory values are not the six plugin credentials and endpoint fields.

choices.text: Tenant name, DCE secret, log filter, CA certificate, UDP port, and group ID
choices.feedback: The DCE URL is not a DCE secret; the listed values do not match the documented profile.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of variable references such as ${CLIENT_SECRET} in the output profile?

choices.text: They replace the DCR transformation at ingestion time
choices.feedback: The DCR transform still defines the target schema and TimeGenerated mapping.

choices.text: They make the App Registration anonymous in this ingestion path
choices.feedback: Azure still authenticates the application; variable indirection does not remove identity.

choices.text: They select which FortiGate logs are collected
choices.feedback: Log selection is controlled by forwarding settings and filters, not secret variables.

choices.text: Variables keep literal secrets out of profile text
choices.feedback: Correct: the Community tip uses variables to mask values such as the client secret.

questions.stem: Azure returns an ingestion schema error after the token succeeds. Which area deserves attention first?

choices.text: DCR stream, custom table schema, and TimeGenerated transformation
choices.feedback: Correct: successful token acquisition moves the fault boundary toward DCR/table schema and transform.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer administrator password expiration for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: An admin password does not explain an authenticated ingestion request rejected for schema.

choices.text: FortiGate BGP neighbor update-source configuration for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: BGP update-source is unrelated to Azure log schema validation.

choices.text: FortiSwitch VRRP preemption timer for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: VRRP preemption does not affect the table schema accepted by Azure.

questions.stem: A FortiSwitch VRRP Master is still sending advertisements, but the upstream route is gone. Which feature addresses this?

choices.text: Lowering the advertisement interval only for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: Faster advertisements detect peer failure, not a live Master that has lost upstream reachability.

choices.text: Changing the virtual router ID on the backup
choices.feedback: Changing the VRID breaks group identity rather than monitoring the route.

choices.text: Configuring vrdst to track a critical destination
choices.feedback: Correct: vrdst monitors destination reachability and can reduce the Master's priority to zero.

choices.text: Disabling the virtual MAC on the primary
choices.feedback: Disabling VMAC can disrupt the shared gateway identity and does not provide route tracking.

questions.stem: What does priority zero in get router info vrrp indicate in the documented route-monitor scenario?

choices.text: The VRRP group has been deleted for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: The group remains configured; priority zero is the route-tracking response.

choices.text: The tracked destination failed; Master priority became zero
choices.feedback: Correct: loss of the monitored destination drives the Master priority to zero.

choices.text: The backup has a higher interface speed for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: Interface speed is not the condition shown by the vrdst example.

choices.text: The virtual IP address has changed to the physical address
choices.feedback: The virtual IP remains the shared gateway; it does not become the physical address.

questions.stem: Which design choice makes a vrdst monitor useful rather than noisy?

choices.text: Choose a critical destination reachable through the intended upstream path
choices.feedback: Correct: the target should represent the path whose loss should trigger gateway failover.

choices.text: Choose a public host that both switches may be unable to ping
choices.feedback: A target unreachable from both peers can make both priorities fall and defeat the design.

choices.text: Choose the switch's own management address on the same VLAN for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: The local management address does not test the upstream route being protected.

choices.text: Choose a host whose ICMP policy changes frequently for this VRRP group
choices.feedback: An unstable ICMP policy can cause false failovers unrelated to actual routing.

questions.stem: Which prerequisite is called out for FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC operation?

choices.text: Enable allow-mac-move on every FS-6xxF first on the AP management path
choices.feedback: On some models allow-mac-move conflicts with VMAC; it is not a universal prerequisite.

choices.text: Use a unique virtual IP on every member
choices.feedback: Members of the same VRRP group share the virtual IP rather than each using a different one.

choices.text: Disable the advanced-features license on the AP management path
choices.feedback: VRRP requires the advanced-features license; disabling it removes the entitlement.

choices.text: Enable VMAC on all members; check model conflicts
choices.feedback: Correct: VMAC is disabled by default and must be enabled across the group, subject to model limits.

questions.stem: FortiGate manages a FortiAP over IPv6. Which interface permission is required for the wireless fabric management path?

choices.text: ip6-allowaccess ping only
choices.feedback: Ping allows ICMP testing but does not enable the wireless fabric management service.

choices.text: ip6-allowaccess fabric
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet's IPv6 management example includes fabric in ip6-allowaccess.

choices.text: allowaccess radius-acct on IPv4
choices.feedback: RADIUS accounting access is unrelated to AP controller discovery over IPv6.

choices.text: set vrrp-virtual-mac enable
choices.feedback: VRRP VMAC is a gateway feature, not a FortiAP management permission.

questions.stem: Which two methods are documented for FortiAP IPv6 controller discovery?

choices.text: DNS SRV and static ARP on the AP management path
choices.feedback: Those are not the two discovery methods documented for IPv6 AP controller discovery.

choices.text: BGP route reflection and LLDP on the AP management path
choices.feedback: Routing and LLDP may support connectivity but are not the discovery mechanisms listed.

choices.text: IPv6 multicast and DHCPv6 Option 52 discovery
choices.feedback: Correct: the AP can discover through controller multicast or DHCPv6 Option 52.

choices.text: SAML redirect and RADIUS CoA on the AP management path
choices.feedback: SAML and CoA belong to identity workflows, not CAPWAP controller discovery.

questions.stem: What does NP7/NP7lite support that NP6/NP6lite does not in this feature?

choices.text: CAPWAP offload for IPv4 and IPv6 data
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet documents CAPWAP data offload on NP7/NP7lite, not NP6/NP6lite.

choices.text: DHCPv6 Option 52 address assignment on the AP management path
choices.feedback: DHCPv6 Option 52 is a discovery method, not an NPU offload capability.

choices.text: IPv6 client SLAAC on the wireless SSID
choices.feedback: Client SLAAC is an IPv6 client service and not the documented hardware boundary.

choices.text: The FortiAP authorization database on the AP management path
choices.feedback: AP authorization is controller logic, not the NPU offload feature.

questions.stem: The AP console shows cwWtpd restarting repeatedly. What is the strongest next step?

choices.text: RMA the AP because the process name proves hardware failure
choices.feedback: A process restart is a symptom and does not establish a hardware defect.

choices.text: Change every SSID to bridge mode in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: SSID forwarding mode does not explain a controller process restarting before stable CAPWAP.

choices.text: Disable CAPWAP encryption without checking compatibility in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Disabling security without evidence is unsafe and may not address the cause.

choices.text: Correlate AP firmware, FSM/crash/certificate/power evidence with an on-network CAPWAP capture
choices.feedback: Correct: collect firmware, FSM, crash, power and certificate evidence plus real network testing.

questions.stem: FortiNAC reports “No EAP session matching state.” What does the message most directly indicate?

choices.text: The user's password has definitely expired in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Credential failure is possible later, but the message describes missing EAP session context.

choices.text: EAP arrived without a matching active server session
choices.feedback: Correct: the server received EAP traffic but could not associate it with a live EAP state.

choices.text: The switch VLAN tag is malformed in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: A VLAN error may affect access after authentication but does not explain this EAP state message.

choices.text: The endpoint has no IPv6 default route
choices.feedback: IPv6 routing is unrelated to the RADIUS/EAP session correlation symptom.

questions.stem: In FortiNAC proxy RADIUS mode, what happens to 802.1X EAP authentication?

choices.text: FortiNAC processes only accounting and drops EAP in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Proxy mode is an authentication path, not a policy to drop EAP.

choices.text: FortiNAC converts EAP into SNMP polling in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: SNMP polling is a separate network-device management mechanism.

choices.text: FortiNAC proxies EAP authentication to an external RADIUS server
choices.feedback: Correct: proxy mode handles MAC auth locally and proxies 802.1X EAP to external RADIUS.

choices.text: FortiNAC assigns a VLAN without consulting an authentication service
choices.feedback: VLAN assignment can follow authorization, but it does not replace EAP authentication.

questions.stem: Which prerequisite applies to FortiNAC Local RADIUS EAP authentication?

choices.text: A server certificate must be installed for EAP
choices.feedback: Correct: the Local RADIUS guide requires a server certificate for EAP authentication.

choices.text: The switch must use BGP multihop in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: BGP multihop is unrelated to the RADIUS EAP service.

choices.text: The FortiNAC Manager must share a VRID with the NAS
choices.feedback: VRID is a VRRP identifier, not a RADIUS requirement.

choices.text: The DCR table must end in _CL in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: _CL is an Azure table naming convention, not an EAP prerequisite.

questions.stem: The same endpoint succeeds off-peak but intermittently loses EAP state during busy periods. Which hypothesis best matches the forum discussion?

choices.text: A permanent VLAN mismatch on every port
choices.feedback: A fixed VLAN error would not normally explain intermittent EAP state correlation.

choices.text: An invalid AP certificate in all cases
choices.feedback: An AP certificate issue is not established by the EAP session message and affects more than one path.

choices.text: A missing BGP route to the RADIUS server
choices.feedback: BGP reachability may affect RADIUS transport, but the stated symptom is a missing active EAP context.

choices.text: Delay, load distribution, or a restarted EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Correct: these are the specific classes of causes raised by Fortinet staff in the recent discussion.

questions.stem: What does FortiNAC Local RADIUS not provide by itself?

choices.text: EAP authentication for supported methods in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Local RADIUS supports documented EAP methods when prerequisites are met.

choices.text: RADIUS accounting; proxy it externally if required
choices.feedback: Correct: Local RADIUS does not provide accounting; it can be proxied externally.

choices.text: MAC authentication processing in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: Local RADIUS processes MAC authentication as well as EAP authentication.

choices.text: RADIUS Access-Accept attributes in this EAP exchange
choices.feedback: FortiNAC can return configured RADIUS attributes in an Access-Accept.

questions.stem: In FortiNAC-F global-object synchronization, which system is authoritative for shared objects?

choices.text: The endpoint supplicant for this global object
choices.feedback: The supplicant is not a configuration authority for FortiNAC global objects.

choices.text: The managed CA's local database row
choices.feedback: Managed CA global objects are read-only and are overwritten from the Manager.

choices.text: FortiNAC Manager
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiNAC Manager owns the shared global-object configuration.

choices.text: The switch's RADIUS client table
choices.feedback: The switch RADIUS table is unrelated to Manager object replication.

questions.stem: A managed CA's Group row ID differs from the Manager's row ID, but the GUID matches. What should the engineer conclude?

choices.text: Local IDs may differ; shared GUID identifies the object
choices.feedback: Correct: local database IDs are appliance-local; the GUID is the cross-appliance identity.

choices.text: The objects are duplicates and both must be deleted
choices.feedback: Different row IDs alone do not prove duplication and deleting global objects is unsafe.

choices.text: The managed CA is running the wrong VRRP group
choices.feedback: VRRP group configuration has no relationship to FortiNAC object identity.

choices.text: The Manager must use the CA's local row ID
choices.feedback: The Manager remains authoritative; local IDs do not need to match.

questions.stem: Which objects are examples of FortiNAC-F global synchronization content?

choices.text: Live packet captures and interface counters
choices.feedback: Packet captures and counters are operational evidence, not the listed global configuration objects.

choices.text: Only local host MAC learning tables
choices.feedback: Host propagation is a separate replication function from global-object synchronization.

choices.text: Only AP radio channel assignments for this global object
choices.feedback: AP radio channels are not the listed FortiNAC-F global objects.

choices.text: Groups, Roles, Admin Profiles, and compliance objects
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide lists Groups, Roles, Admin Profiles, and compliance objects.

questions.stem: A GUID conflict is confirmed for one global Group on a managed CA. What is the safe repair posture?

choices.text: Run a broad UPDATE on every Group row for this global object
choices.feedback: A broad update can damage valid global and local-only objects.

choices.text: Back up, compare GUIDs, repair only the stale CA row
choices.feedback: Correct: back up, compare exact objects, and perform a narrowly scoped repair with Support guidance.

choices.text: Change the Manager GUID to match the CA local ID
choices.feedback: The Manager is authoritative; changing its GUID to a local ID reverses the authority model.

choices.text: Delete all local-only groups before synchronizing for this global object
choices.feedback: Local-only objects must not be altered as part of a global-object repair.

questions.stem: A TACACS+ request reaches FortiAuthenticator, but the NAS sends authorization before authentication. What is the core issue?

choices.text: The user group lacks a VLAN ID
choices.feedback: VLAN assignment is not the core TACACS+ sequence issue.

choices.text: The server DNS suffix is missing
choices.feedback: DNS may affect reachability but does not change TACACS+ request ordering.

choices.text: The NAS sends authorization before authentication
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiAuthenticator does not provide an authorization-before-authentication mode for this flow.

choices.text: The RADIUS shared secret is too short
choices.feedback: A RADIUS shared secret is not the TACACS+ phase-order issue.

questions.stem: Before FortiAuthenticator accepts TACACS+ requests, what must exist?

choices.text: A FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC for this TACACS+ client
choices.feedback: VRRP is unrelated to TACACS+ client registration.

choices.text: Register the NAS and assign its TACACS+ policy
choices.feedback: Correct: the TACACS+ device must be registered and assigned to a policy.

choices.text: An Azure Data Collection Rule for this TACACS+ client
choices.feedback: A DCR is an Azure log-ingestion object, not an authentication prerequisite.

choices.text: A FortiPAM secret template for this TACACS+ client
choices.feedback: FortiPAM secret templates do not configure FortiAuthenticator TACACS+.

questions.stem: Where does FortiAuthenticator expose TACACS+ service debug logs?

choices.text: System > SD-WAN > Health Check
choices.feedback: SD-WAN health checks do not expose FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ logs.

choices.text: FortiManager Install Preview for this TACACS+ client
choices.feedback: Install Preview belongs to FortiManager device configuration deployment.

choices.text: FortiAnalyzer Log Forwarding > Output Profile
choices.feedback: Output Profile is a FortiAnalyzer log-forwarding feature.

choices.text: Open /debug/ and select TACACS+
choices.feedback: Correct: open /debug/ and select TACACS+ from the service dropdown.

questions.stem: What is the documented FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ limitation for two-factor authentication?

choices.text: Append the OTP to the password; no challenge flow
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiAuthenticator documents token-appended password entry because TACACS+ challenge/response is unsupported.

choices.text: Use a browser SAML redirect after every command
choices.feedback: SAML redirects are not the documented TACACS+ 2FA method.

choices.text: Send the token as a RADIUS Tunnel-Private-Group-Id for this TACACS+ client
choices.feedback: Tunnel-Private-Group-Id is a RADIUS VLAN attribute, not TACACS+ OTP handling.

choices.text: Require a client certificate on every SSH command
choices.feedback: A client certificate is not the stated TACACS+ 2FA mechanism.

questions.stem: A FortiPAM REST request uses a client certificate and bearer token. What does each prove?

choices.text: Both prove only the user's password for this protected secret at the API gateway
choices.feedback: A password is not what either artifact represents in this design.

choices.text: The certificate proves API role membership; the token proves the EMS tag
choices.feedback: The certificate is used for client trust; the token identifies the API user.

choices.text: The certificate and token are interchangeable methods for this protected secret
choices.feedback: They are independent gates, not interchangeable alternatives.

choices.text: The certificate establishes endpoint trust; the bearer token authenticates the API user
choices.feedback: Correct: device trust and API identity are separate controls.

questions.stem: FortiPAM ZTNA is enabled, but a managed endpoint cannot launch a protected secret. Which check is especially important?

choices.text: Confirm same EMS and the expected endpoint tag
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiPAM tag control depends on the same EMS control plane and matching posture tag.

choices.text: The SD-WAN quota counter has reset for this protected secret
choices.feedback: Quota counters do not determine FortiPAM secret access.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch VRRP priority is 255 for this protected secret
choices.feedback: VRRP priority is unrelated to endpoint posture.

choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer DCR table has TimeGenerated for this protected secret
choices.feedback: Azure table schema does not authorize a FortiPAM secret launch.

questions.stem: What does the /pam URL map in the FortiPAM access proxy do?

choices.text: It changes the API user's bearer token
choices.feedback: The API token is generated for the API user and is not changed by URL mapping.

choices.text: Map /pam requests to the pam-service gateway
choices.feedback: Correct: the API gateway maps /pam to the FortiPAM service.

choices.text: It creates the EMS endpoint tag automatically
choices.feedback: EMS tags are created/evaluated by endpoint management, not URL maps.

choices.text: It disables client certificate validation for this protected secret
choices.feedback: Client certificate behavior is controlled separately in the access proxy.

questions.stem: FortiPAM login succeeds but access to one secret is denied. Which control may still block the operation?

choices.text: The FortiSIEM offline repository mount
choices.feedback: The offline repo is unrelated to privileged secret authorization.

choices.text: The FortiSwitch tracked destination
choices.feedback: VRRP route tracking does not authorize a PAM secret.

choices.text: The Windows DNS priority list
choices.feedback: DNS priority may affect name resolution, not the secret permission decision.

choices.text: Secret-level ZTNA and secret permissions
choices.feedback: Correct: secret-level ZTNA and secret permissions are separate from appliance login.

questions.stem: For FortiSIEM 7.5.1 offline OS repository preparation, what storage requirement is documented?

choices.text: At least 2 TB on the mounted staging filesystem
choices.feedback: Correct: the 7.5.1 guide specifies at least 2 TB for the OS repository.

choices.text: At least 2 GB on the Supervisor root partition
choices.feedback: 2 GB is far below the documented repository requirement.

choices.text: A 375 GB temporary directory only in this offline upgrade
choices.feedback: 375 GB belongs to earlier version documentation and must not be reused for 7.5.1.

choices.text: No local storage because the ZIP contains all OS packages
choices.feedback: The OS repository is a separate dependency from the main upgrade ZIP.

questions.stem: Why extract fsm-sync-os-repo.sh from the targeted upgrade package?

choices.text: The script configures FortiGate BGP neighbors in this offline upgrade
choices.feedback: The script builds the FortiSIEM OS repository, not BGP configuration.

choices.text: It matches the target upgrade release
choices.feedback: Correct: the Community tip recommends extracting the script from the target version's upgrade RPM.

choices.text: The script creates a new RADIUS client secret
choices.feedback: RADIUS client secrets are unrelated to repository synchronization.

choices.text: The script replaces the Supervisor database in this offline upgrade
choices.feedback: The repository script does not replace the FortiSIEM database.

questions.stem: Which command tells the Supervisor upgrade to use the mounted offline repository?

choices.text: ./upgrade.sh --proxy-only /repo
choices.feedback: The documented parameter is not a proxy-only option.

choices.text: ./upgrade.sh --skip-database-check
choices.feedback: Skipping database checks is not the offline repository selector.

choices.text: ./upgrade.sh --offline-osrepo-path /offline-repo
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide documents --offline-osrepo-path with the mounted repository path.

choices.text: ./upgrade.sh --disable-wget
choices.feedback: Disabling wget is not how the upgrade script selects offline packages.

questions.stem: After Supervisor is upgraded, what extra value does a Worker upgrade consume?

choices.text: The FortiGate remote AS number
choices.feedback: The BGP remote AS is unrelated to FortiSIEM Worker updates.

choices.text: The FortiPAM API bearer token
choices.feedback: FortiPAM API credentials do not authorize FortiSIEM OS package access.

choices.text: The FortiAuthenticator TACACS+ shared secret
choices.feedback: TACACS+ shared secrets do not participate in the Worker upgrade.

choices.text: The Supervisor's offline-repository password
choices.feedback: Correct: the Worker script uses the Supervisor's offline-repository OS update password.

questions.stem: What is the Multi-Connect feature limitation documented for FortiClient?

choices.text: Only SSL VPN tunnels can connect concurrently
choices.feedback: SSL VPN is not the documented eligible tunnel type for this beta feature.

choices.text: Only IKEv2 IPsec tunnels qualify; feature is beta
choices.feedback: Correct: the guide limits Multi-Connect to eligible IPsec IKEv2 tunnels and marks it beta.

choices.text: Only one tunnel can be configured per profile
choices.feedback: The profile can list up to 50 eligible IKEv2 tunnels.

choices.text: It supports every tunnel protocol without version constraints
choices.feedback: The feature has explicit tunnel-type and platform constraints.

questions.stem: What does DNS Priority control on Windows when Multi-Connect is enabled?

choices.text: Which tunnel receives all application traffic regardless of routing
choices.feedback: DNS priority is not a general packet steering policy for every application flow.

choices.text: Which tunnel is allowed to negotiate IKE first
choices.feedback: IKE negotiation order is not what the DNS priority list configures.

choices.text: Windows DNS resolver priority across tunnel interfaces
choices.feedback: Correct: Windows queries the DNS server on the highest-priority tunnel first, then tries the next if needed.

choices.text: The FortiSASE PoP server certificate for this IKEv2 tunnel
choices.feedback: PoP certificate selection is unrelated to endpoint DNS resolver order.

questions.stem: A user reports the SASE tunnel is up but the on-prem tunnel is down. What is the right diagnostic approach?

choices.text: Assume the endpoint profile was not received for this IKEv2 tunnel
choices.feedback: A working SASE tunnel suggests the profile may have reached the endpoint.

choices.text: Edit the FortiSASE-owned Phase 1 and Phase 2 settings
choices.feedback: FortiSASE service-owned Phase 1/2 settings are not editable through that interface.

choices.text: Disable the SASE tunnel for every endpoint for this IKEv2 tunnel
choices.feedback: Disabling the SASE service is not a diagnosis of the separate custom tunnel.

choices.text: Check each tunnel separately and validate custom IKEv2 settings
choices.feedback: Correct: SASE and custom IKEv2 tunnels have separate ownership and negotiation state.

questions.stem: Why must an on-prem gateway match the endpoint's custom-tunnel parameters?

choices.text: FortiSASE configures specific IKEv2 proposals and lifetimes on FortiClient
choices.feedback: Correct: the tunnel settings guide lists endpoint parameters the remote gateway must match.

choices.text: The gateway inherits the FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC for this IKEv2 tunnel
choices.feedback: VRRP virtual MAC is not an IPsec proposal parameter.

choices.text: The custom tunnel uses the Azure DCR identifier as its peer ID
choices.feedback: DCR IDs belong to Azure log ingestion, not IKE identity.

choices.text: Windows DNS Priority rewrites the Phase 2 proposal for this IKEv2 tunnel
choices.feedback: DNS priority controls resolver order and does not rewrite IKE/Phase 2 negotiation.

questions.stem: The FortiSASE tunnel's Phase 1/2 settings are not editable in the console. What is the correct interpretation?

choices.text: The endpoint has lost its EMS tag for this SD-WAN service
choices.feedback: An EMS tag issue affects posture/authorization, not tunnel-setting ownership.

choices.text: The tunnel is using SSL VPN instead of IKEv2
choices.feedback: Missing edit controls do not indicate a change in VPN protocol.

choices.text: SASE owns its tunnel settings; configure custom tunnels separately
choices.feedback: Correct: the Community clarification says SASE Phase 1/2 settings cannot be changed there.

choices.text: The API bearer token has expired for this SD-WAN service
choices.feedback: API tokens are unrelated to service-owned IPsec parameters.

questions.stem: What is the key role of quota-limit on an SD-WAN member?

choices.text: It sets the interface MTU for this SD-WAN service during the billing period
choices.feedback: MTU is a separate interface setting.

choices.text: It defines a monthly traffic-volume threshold in gigabytes
choices.feedback: Correct: quota-limit sets the volume threshold used for monthly overage steering.

choices.text: It forces the member physically down when the ISP link is up
choices.feedback: The member can remain alive; the feature adjusts selection preference.

choices.text: It caps every packet to a fixed bandwidth rate for this SD-WAN service
choices.feedback: The quota feature is not a hard rate limiter or per-packet shaper.

questions.stem: Which command inspects quota/overage state for one SD-WAN member?

choices.text: diagnose sys sdwan bill member <id>
choices.feedback: Correct: FortiOS 8.0 adds the SD-WAN bill member diagnostic.

choices.text: get router info vrrp for this SD-WAN service
choices.feedback: That command displays VRRP state, not billing counters.

choices.text: diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp
choices.feedback: The wireless controller command is not the quota diagnostic.

choices.text: execute tacacs test user for this SD-WAN service
choices.feedback: TACACS user testing is unrelated to SD-WAN member usage.

questions.stem: A member is over quota but traffic remains on it. What should be checked with billing output?

choices.text: Whether the BGP neighbor is in OpenConfirm
choices.feedback: BGP state does not establish the member's quota accounting state.

choices.text: Whether the FortiPAM certificate is valid
choices.feedback: FortiPAM certificate validation does not affect SD-WAN quota counters.

choices.text: Check overage state and the enabled flag
choices.feedback: Correct: verify threshold, billing start day, overage enablement, and current overaged state.

choices.text: Whether the FortiNAC EAP session has expired
choices.feedback: EAP session state is unrelated to SD-WAN member selection.
